_meta.purpose: Compact, machine-readable per-module capability overview: question, model class, assumptions, evidence type, verification scripts, known limits. Written 2026-09-24 in response to Astra's capability-assessment review (prompts/Answers/nicht_stationäre_Treiber/SCF_Faehigkeiten_und_Ausbauplan_2026-09-24.md, Priority 0) as the README's headline claims should only ever summarize what is stated here.
_meta.as_of_commit: Paket C1 (hydrology state estimation, integrated extension roadmap)

modules.question: Do a state map and a time map between two models preserve dynamics, and how large is the residual?
modules.model_class: Abstract contract (dataclasses + residual functions) over user-supplied maps.
modules.assumptions: Maps and dynamics are supplied by the caller; checked only on sampled state-time pairs, not proven globally.
modules.known_limits: A certificate on sampled points is not a global equivalence proof.

modules.question: How much information survives observation, and is it redundant, unique, or synergistic across sources?
modules.model_class: Discrete channel capacity (Arimoto-Blahut), directed information, finite-context representability.
modules.assumptions: Finite alphabets/discretization; results depend on chosen distributions and information decomposition.
modules.known_limits: Information dependence alone does not establish causality; no real-world dataset used here.

modules.question: How do feedback, recovery, hysteresis, and driving rate produce transitions in selected model systems?
modules.model_class: Cubic normal form, contraction, Landau/Ising, GSPT, Floquet, panarchy cusp, early warning, rate-dependent tipping, energy-balance climate model, ETAS earthquake model.
modules.assumptions: Each submodel has its own scope (e.g. slow/fast separation for GSPT, subcriticality for ETAS stationarity).
modules.evidence_type: mixed: analytic normal forms + two real-data pilots (energy balance on Mauna Loa CO2 + NOAA temperature; ETAS on USGS earthquakes)
modules.known_limits: No universal tipping-point detector; the rate-dependent χ diagnostic is direction-correct across the tested range but its precise numeric threshold was found to be grid-resolution-dependent, not exact (see NONSTATIONARY_ROADMAP.md package 4). Energy-balance parameters C_s/C_d/alpha are weakly constrained on a ±50% scan around the fit, not proven globally unidentifiable (see docs/energy_balance.md).

modules.question: Which couplings represent influence, transport, energy-conserving, or dissipative exchange between systems?
modules.model_class: Coupling layers, Casimir/Dirac composition, dissipativity, GENERIC-Navier-Stokes bridge, generalized synchronization.
modules.assumptions: Specific structural conditions (e.g. GENERIC degeneracy conditions) must hold and are checked per example, not assumed to generalize.
modules.known_limits: Structural checks on selected examples are not a blanket physical validation of arbitrary coupled systems.

modules.question: When can an aggregated (macro) model be described self-sufficiently, and when does it need hidden state or memory?
modules.model_class: PC=CQ macro-closure, generator lumpability, Chapman-Enskog reduction, propagated error bounds.
modules.assumptions: Exact closure requires specific lumpability/commutation conditions that are checked, not assumed.
modules.known_limits: No general data-driven reduction pipeline with automatically identified memory kernels. Priority 3 (docs/linear_memory_projection.md) adds an exact Mori-Zwanzig-style memory reduction for LINEAR systems (arbitrary hidden dimension): the memoryless (Markov) approximation is beaten on mean error, minimum value/time, AND boundary-crossing time by a finite-memory approximation on a stable worked example. Nonlinear hidden-state elimination remains out of scope. Package 6 (Astra second review, SCF_Review_dc5d82a.md) fixed two real bugs: a NumPy >=2.4 incompatibility (float() of a 1-element array, removed np.trapz) that made CI genuinely red, and a local-vs-global minimum bug (single scipy.optimize.minimize_scalar bracket search missed the true extremum on oscillating trajectories) -- fixed via analytic spline stationary points plus adaptive sampling.

modules.question: When do loads, reserves, and coupled resource conditions violate a defined safety boundary?
modules.model_class: Viability kernels, Nagumo tangent cones, scalar control barrier functions, rate-dependent buffer spikes, multidimensional tipping/reserve maps.
modules.assumptions: Safety is defined relative to an explicit boundary, model class, and time span; the control-barrier example is scalar.
modules.evidence_type: analytic + independently hand-derived closed-form regression checks (see verify_multidim_tipping_maps.py's Gaussian-pulse convolution check)
modules.known_limits: Buffer-minimum localization was found to have grid-search error ≫ ODE-tolerance error in one adversarial case; fixed via continuous optimization, see MECHANISTIC_VALIDATION_ROADMAP.md package 6a. Priority 4 (docs/transient_amplification.md) adds a DIFFERENT tipping mechanism: a stable (all-negative-eigenvalue) 2x2 non-normal coupling can transiently amplify a perturbation across a safety boundary with no unstable eigenvalue and no growing driver — classified rigorously (from eigenvalues, not simulation alone) as transient (guaranteed return) vs. no-guaranteed-return, restricted to 2x2 linear systems. Package 6 (Astra second review) fixed a real local-vs-global minimum bug (a single scipy.optimize.minimize_scalar bracket search silently missed the true peak on an oscillating system, reporting 'safe' when the true peak exceeded the boundary) and renamed safe_no_violation to no_violation_in_horizon to make clear this is not a permanent safety claim. Package 7 (Astra6.txt) found the Package-6 fix still missed FAST NON-oscillating spikes (adaptive sampling only considered eigenvalues' imaginary parts, not large real parts) -- fixed by also resolving fast real decay/growth rates, and more fundamentally by making the peak search in classify_two_buffer_transient exact and sampling-independent: every component of a homogeneous 2x2 system satisfies the same 2nd-order constant-coefficient ODE from A's characteristic polynomial, solved in closed form for all three eigenvalue cases. Priority 5 (docs/coupled_buffer_cbf_qp.md) extends the scalar control-barrier example to two buffers with a shared resource budget: a minimal-cost CBF-QP intervention is compared against no-intervention and a naive fixed rule, with TWO distinct infeasibility modes (a single buffer's own bounds vs. the shared budget) surfaced explicitly via an independent closed-form certificate. Package 6 separated instantaneous CBF satisfaction (cbf_condition_satisfied_now) from sustained trajectory safety (sustained_safe_until_horizon, computed from the exact held-control closed form) after Astra showed the cheapest instantaneous solution can violate a buffer shortly after being applied. Package 7 fixed two edge-case bugs in that same sustained-safety check (an already-negative start state was misreported safe; a trajectory touching zero exactly at the horizon was misreported unsafe) via an exact endpoint-minimum reformulation. Two buffers only, identity/linear-class-K barrier only.

modules.question: How do systems classify into overlapping categories, and what concept lattice do their attributes induce?
modules.model_class: Membership matrices, Formal Concept Analysis.
modules.assumptions: Finite, explicitly given attribute sets.
modules.known_limits: Small reference examples; no real-data application yet.

modules.question: Given a model and data, which parameters are pinned down by the data and which are not?
modules.model_class: Profile likelihood (1D golden-section and multi-parameter bounded NLP), Fisher-information sloppiness spectra.
modules.assumptions: Confidence-interval claims are always relative to the actually scanned grid/range.
modules.evidence_type: analytic worked examples + applied to real-data fits (energy balance, ETAS)
modules.known_limits: `likelihood_interval` never returns `established_unbounded=True` from grid data alone (2026-09-23 correction, package 9): a profile flat on the scanned grid can still have a bounded true confidence set just beyond it. `flat_in_scanned_range` is the honest, scan-relative field to use instead.

modules.question: Do mechanistic models beat simple statistical baselines out-of-sample, with honestly reported point AND interval performance?
modules.model_class: Rolling-origin backtesting, split conformal prediction, mechanistic probabilistic evaluation (leave-one-origin-out intervals), COVID country decomposition/observation models, Cygnus X-1 pilot.
modules.assumptions: Each origin uses only information available at that origin; look-ahead in calibration is explicitly guarded against (strict temporal eligibility, package 7).
modules.evidence_type: real data: OWID/JHU COVID series, NOAA global temperature anomaly, USGS earthquakes M≥6.0; Cygnus X-1 radio epochs are explicitly flagged unverified/illustrative (likely AI-interpolated, not archived raw measurements)
modules.known_limits: Nominal 80% prediction intervals achieved only 52.5% empirical coverage (energy balance, n=40 cases) and 26.3% (COVID renewal, n=19 cases) via the original leave-one-origin-out (signed lo/hi quantile) construction. A separate symmetric absolute-residual quantile construction (Priority 1, docs/adaptive_interval_calibration.md) gets 70-85% on energy balance but 0% for COVID persistence (residuals grow monotonically during 2020 exponential onset, so no past-only quantile can catch up) — comparing three calibration variants (fixed rolling reference, Adaptive Conformal Inference, a P+I subset of Conformal PID Control) shows the adaptive recursions help on a controlled synthetic regime-shift example but neither clearly help nor hurt on these small real pilots (n=19-40). Best interval score does not imply best coverage. Package 6 (Astra second review) fixed a real future-information leak in the ACI/PID adaptation state under overlapping forecast horizons (a trial's own outcome was applied to alpha_t before its own target time had actually elapsed relative to a later origin) and documented that even the fixed recursion does not inherit Gibbs & Candes's long-run coverage guarantee once alpha_t is numerically clipped (a strictly increasing error sequence gives 0% coverage forever). Priority 2 (docs/covid_latent_renewal_observation.md): a full 2x2 ablation (Package 6) shows negative-binomial overdispersion ALONE is the strong finding (2.4% -> 73.8% coverage, log-score 1387 -> 10.2 on 42 held-out trials, renewal dynamics held fixed); the weekday reporting correction on top actually WORSENS both metrics on this window -- corrected from an earlier framing that bundled both changes together. True reporting-delay (a report-date x episode-date matrix) remains out of scope — the OWID/JHU series has no such matrix.

modules.question: Can a set of declared local probability models be represented by one global model (sheaf-theoretic contextuality)?
modules.model_class: Sheaf contextuality, Čech cohomology obstructions, CSW graph invariants.
modules.assumptions: Finite measurement/outcome spaces; externally reviewed optional module (F08).
modules.evidence_type: analytic worked examples, checksums/script runs independently re-verified
modules.known_limits: Small reference examples; optional module, does not affect the core contract.

modules.question: How does joint information from multiple sources about a target split into redundant, unique, and synergistic parts?
modules.model_class: Partial Information Decomposition (Williams-Beer, Kolchinsky redundancy bottleneck), BROJA.
modules.assumptions: Finite discrete source/target distributions; externally reviewed optional module (F09).
modules.known_limits: Optional module; decomposition choice affects numeric results (known open problem in the PID literature generally, not specific to this repo).

modules.question: Which network structures satisfy nonequilibrium thermodynamic consistency (entropy production, detailed/complex balance)?
modules.model_class: Schnakenberg network thermodynamics, Crooks/Jarzynski fluctuation relations.
modules.assumptions: Markov network structure with specified rate constants.
modules.known_limits: Small reference networks; no real thermodynamic experiment data used.

modules.question: Which subsets of a reaction network are self-maintaining and closed under production (a 'chemical organization')?
modules.model_class: Chemical Organization Theory.
modules.assumptions: Fixed, explicitly given reaction network.
modules.known_limits: Single small reference example.

modules.question: At what branching/connection probability does a Bethe-lattice-like structure percolate?
modules.model_class: Bethe-tree percolation / Kesten branching-process threshold.
modules.assumptions: Infinite regular tree approximation.
modules.known_limits: Idealized tree structure, not a finite real network.

modules.question: Under what diffusion/reaction parameters does a Turing instability produce spatial patterns?
modules.model_class: Turing instability / dispersion relation analysis.
modules.assumptions: Linear stability analysis around a homogeneous steady state.
modules.known_limits: Linear analysis only; no nonlinear pattern simulation.

modules.question: How does a moving phase boundary (e.g. melting front) evolve under a self-similar Stefan condition?
modules.model_class: Stefan-Neumann similarity solution.
modules.assumptions: One-dimensional, self-similar geometry.
modules.known_limits: Single idealized geometry.

modules.question: Which cross-repository conventions (scope declarations, error handling, provenance) must every module follow?
modules.model_class: Meta-level rule checks, not a domain model.
modules.assumptions: None domain-specific; enforces repo-wide discipline.
modules.known_limits: Enforces process discipline, not a scientific claim in itself.

modules.question: Do the original Revision 2/3 worked examples (pre-package era) still reproduce?
modules.model_class: Adapters to the original standalone verification scripts.
modules.assumptions: Historical scope as originally defined in Revision 2/3 documents.
modules.known_limits: Frozen historical scope; superseded conceptually by the installable package's own modules where overlapping.

modules.question: When does a time-averaged load description lose the information needed for a short-term capacity event, and how likely is a capacity breach under the SAME mean rates?
modules.model_class: Deterministic reflected fluid backlog (piecewise-constant rates, exact per-segment monotonicity); M/M/1 CTMC restricted to an absorbing-generator first-passage construction.
modules.assumptions: Single server/stock, piecewise-constant rates (deterministic side); Poisson arrivals / exponential service, single server (stochastic side). No network/priority queues.
modules.evidence_type: synthetic/analytic; Astra's fixed worked example and CTMC reference value reproduced independently to <1e-12, plus an independent event-driven simulation and solve_ivp/Poisson cross-checks
modules.known_limits: DOMAIN_EXPANSION_ROADMAP.md Paket B2: for rho=0.5<1 (stable mean), the deterministic fluid model reports peak backlog exactly 0 while the stochastic model with the SAME mean rates gives P(hit K)~5.6% -- a mean/fluid statement is never a stochastic safety proof. A real trace-driven pilot (plan section 8.4) is explicitly deferred.

modules.question: Does a model with two discharge time scales improve on a single reservoir under the same input and observation, and is the split identifiable? -- now answered on real German catchments, not only synthetically.
modules.model_class: Parallel linear reservoirs (dS_j/dt = alpha_j*u - k_j*S_j), exact closed-form update and Mori-Zwanzig-style convolution kernel.
modules.assumptions: Linear reservoirs only -- no nonlinear runoff, snow, or evapotranspiration processes.
modules.evidence_type: synthetic/analytic (reservoir mechanics, cross-checked against solve_ivp); real data pilot on 6 CAMELS-DE catchments (CC-BY-4.0), reproduced once during development and committed as small derived CSV excerpts under data/camels_de/ with full manifest provenance
modules.known_limits: DOMAIN_EXPANSION_ROADMAP.md Paket B3a: k1=k2 and alpha2=0 both reduce to the single-reservoir case; different initial storage splits with the SAME total S0 are demonstrably NOT identifiable from the observed total alone. Paket B3b (response to SCF_Review_fcc9a43.md finding R7): the earlier 'blocked, single 2.18GB archive' assessment was wrong -- the archive's host honors HTTP Range requests, extracting 6 selected catchments' timeseries with <20MB transferred. Real result: persistence beats all four compared models (seasonal, 1-reservoir, 2-reservoir) on all 6 catchments in raw MAE (an honest negative result, and an expected hydrological pattern for a once-fit, non-updated conceptual model over a full decade) -- but the 2-reservoir model consistently beats the 1-reservoir model on all 6 catchments, answering the actual time-scale question independently of the persistence comparison. Low-flow-window comparison between 1- and 2-reservoir is genuinely mixed (2 wins, 4 losses). Six catchments, one country/climate regime -- not claimed representative; see docs/hydrology_pilot.md for full tables.

modules.question: Does a positive expected reserve imply a low probability of touching a lower boundary at some point along the way?
modules.model_class: Brownian motion with drift, exact lower-barrier first-passage probability via the classical reflection-principle formula, log-space stable.
modules.assumptions: Constant drift and diffusion coefficient; no reflection, jumps, or state-dependent noise.
modules.evidence_type: synthetic/analytic; plan's fixed control values reproduced exactly, unit-scaling invariance confirmed over 12 orders of magnitude, independent Euler-Maruyama Monte Carlo cross-check
modules.known_limits: DOMAIN_EXPANSION_ROADMAP.md Paket B4: x0=1, mu=1, sigma=1, H=1 has E[X_1]=2 (comfortably positive) yet P(hit 0 by H=1)~9% -- a genuine, non-negligible breach probability invisible to any statement about the mean trajectory alone. Infinite-horizon ever-hitting probability is a DIFFERENT statement, never extrapolated from a finite scan.

modules.question: When does a nonlinear capacity-aging model improve prediction over linear/persistence references, and how much does observation correlation alone explain?
modules.model_class: Phenomenological mean capacity models (persistence/linear/power-law) kept separate from a 2x2 independent-vs-AR(1) observation ablation; dataset-agnostic per-cell temporal-holdout pilot.
modules.assumptions: Irreversible aging, reversible effects, and measurement error are NOT claimed separately identifiable from a single capacity series -- deliberately restricted to phenomenological mean models.
modules.evidence_type: synthetic-only automated CI (exact recovery, censoring, leakage guards); a real local run against 4 NASA PCoE cells was performed once during development and reported as a manual, non-CI reproduction (see docs/battery_aging_pilot.md)
modules.known_limits: DOMAIN_EXPANSION_ROADMAP.md Paket B5: NASA's own catalog reports the dataset's license as unspecified (independently confirmed via its CKAN API) -- raw/derived per-cycle data are NOT committed to this repo and no manifest entry was added. The real local run (mixed result: linear wins on 2 of 4 cells, power-law on 2, persistence never wins; one genuine right-censoring case) is not independently re-verifiable by a reader without redownloading the same archive.

modules.question: When does additional communicated information improve a joint decision, when is it redundant, and how does channel noise change the answer?
modules.model_class: Three fully-enumerated finite communication tasks (XOR/complementary information, redundancy, noisy channel), evaluated against the EXISTING BROJA bivariate PID solver (information_decomposition/broja.py).
modules.assumptions: Small, exactly enumerable finite tasks only; the sending decision is fixed across all states (never conditioned on the observation).
modules.evidence_type: exact full enumeration (never sampling) of every task state; PID atoms computed by the repo's own unmodified solver, not asserted from a formula
modules.known_limits: DOMAIN_EXPANSION_ROADMAP.md Paket B6a: results are precise answers about the specific manipulated game environment only -- explicitly not human cognition, consciousness, or a general intelligence measure. Repeated/dynamic tasks with delayed feedback and LLM-agent extensions (plan section 12.4) are deliberately deferred.

modules.question: Does a Kalman state correction using the actual daily-mean discharge help a mechanistic reservoir model -- including on real catchments?
modules.model_class: Linear-Gaussian Kalman filter (predict/update, Joseph-form covariance, no explicit matrix inverse) connected to dynamics/linear_reservoirs.py via the exact daily-mean measurement operator (H_Delta, D_Delta derived from the same closed forms as reservoir_interval_discharge).
modules.assumptions: Linear-Gaussian noise model; process noise scale and measurement noise variance are calibrated per catchment/reservoir-count from training data only (inner time-ordered validation), not physically derived; unconstrained (storage can go negative).
modules.evidence_type: hand-verified control case + independent joint-Gaussian-conditioning cross-check (never the same filter function called against itself); real data pilot on the same 6 CAMELS-DE catchments as validation/hydrology_pilot.py
modules.known_limits: INTEGRATED_EXTENSION_ROADMAP.md Paket C1: measurement correction reduces MAE substantially vs. the open-loop model at ALL 6 catchments and all 3 lead times (1/3/7 days), but beats the persistence baseline outright at only 1 of 6 (DEA11490). The inner-validation noise calibration always selects the LARGEST tested process-noise scale (w_scale=1e6) -- checked to be a genuine saturating plateau, not an artifact of too narrow a grid. The unconstrained Gaussian filter produces negative posterior storage on a non-trivial fraction of days at every catchment (reported explicitly, never clipped). Observability diagnostics (observability_matrix/observability_report) are control-case verified but not separately run on the fitted per-catchment (F,H) pairs. A metadata-pre-selected independent confirmation panel (C1c) is explicitly deferred -- see docs/hydrology_state_estimation.md.
